workshops.title: Two ways to celebrate: particles or a bounded MultiMesh
workshops.reason: Critique #6: 'Particles are missing: one small emitter exercise.' This hall is where the project already replaced a particle node with a bounded MultiMesh, so the comparison is the hall's own decision.
workshops.make: A one-shot GPUParticles3D burst with a ParticleProcessMaterial and an emissive draw-pass mesh, fired by the exit gate's opened signal; local versus world coordinates on a moving emitter; the visibility AABB. Then the hall's own choice: a bounded MultiMesh burst with a fixed instance count and lifetime. Compare both under the room's Compatibility renderer.
workshops.check: The burst plays once per opening; the MultiMesh burst stays within its instance count.
workshops.contrast: one_shot off: a fountain. local_coords on a moving emitter: the trail moves with it.
workshops.basis: [M] The arch builds a GPUParticles3D named AtmosphereParticles (rainbow.gd l.226). The celebration frees it (rainbow_celebration.gd l.31: arch.get_node("AtmosphereParticles").queue_free()) and draws MultiMesh confetti (l.17) and sparks, 'Ballistic sparks ... in all renderers. One small MultiMesh per collection' (rainbow_spark_burst.gd l.2-3). All tracked. [D] GPU particle collision is unsupported under Compatibility.

workshops.title: A settings panel
workshops.reason: The palette panel is the room's second panel, and Grid_Pallet already pairs hue with a mark for access. Split from the draft's single menu workshop.
workshops.make: A settings panel reached from the pause menu: MarginContainer, VBoxContainer and HBoxContainer rows; a Theme with a font whose size is the text-size setting; a mouse-sensitivity HSlider the player script reads; anchors so the panel survives a window resize. Applied at once, not yet saved (saving comes at Pattern_Foundry and AirMusic).
workshops.check: Change the text size and sensitivity, close the panel, keep moving: both hold. Resize the window: the panel stays readable.
workshops.contrast: Fixed offsets without containers: the panel breaks at another window size.
workshops.basis: [M] ui.layout and access.a11y are never taught. [M] the survey's access.a11y use: 'volume and mute, and readable font sizes'.

workshops.title: The game in the headset
workshops.reason: The first stop after the room has a menu (W10), settings (W13) and a world-interaction ray (Color_Paint), which are the three things a headset player needs in a different form. Without it the headset route could show the room but not play it.
workshops.make: In my_room's headset copy: install XR Tools 4.5.1 (the course project's version); XRToolsPlayerBody added to group 'player' and put on the player's collision layer, so the collectibles, gate and fields the learner wrote accept it; a direct movement provider and a turn provider; the pause and settings panels shown on a quad through a SubViewport and operated with XRToolsFunctionPointer; a comfort choice (snap or smooth turn, a vignette); the controller ray paints the Color_Paint wall.
workshops.check: Every mechanic from W07 onward works with the headset body without edits; the pointer operates the pause menu; the chosen turn mode applies.
workshops.contrast: A CanvasLayer HUD does not appear in the headset view [K, not run]: the panels have to be in the world.
workshops.basis: [M] addons/godot-xr-tools/player/player_body.gd l.3-4: class_name XRToolsPlayerBody extends CharacterBody3D (gitignored, 4.5.1 per day-zero.md l.42). [M] The survey's ui.world_space change level: 'Builds an interactive 3D panel (XR Tools Viewport2Din3D or its own raycast)'.

workshops.title: Many rooms and a hub
workshops.reason: After CP4 (course exit A) the room has two scenes and a session owner, and the next sequences add heavy systems. Change_Intro's own subject is a rate stated per exhibit.
workshops.make: Reorganise my_room: rooms/<sequence>/<exhibit>.tscn, one scene per exhibit; shared/ for player.tscn, door.tscn and Session.gd; a hub room whose W05 doors lead to each exhibit through change_scene_to_file; 'Save Branch as Scene' to split what has grown inside room.tscn; unique names (%Name) where paths broke. From here every stop starts a new exhibit scene. Commit the move as one change.
workshops.check: Every exhibit opens from the hub and runs alone with F6; the Monitors for one exhibit no longer include the others.
workshops.contrast: Move a scene file outside the FileSystem dock: its uid or path links break; moved inside the dock, they hold.
workshops.basis: [M] In the draft 99 of 111 stops added to one room, and heavy items (a 17x17 floor, per-cell CA bodies, an 8000-cube sponge, a marching-cubes field, 2000 boids) would have measured each other.

workshops.title: A check that runs without you
workshops.reason: Act3's integrator carries an exact claim to check. CLAUDE.md asks for 'a negative test proving the new behavior actually bites'.
workshops.make: Two routes to one check. In the editor: checks/integrator_check.tscn, run with F6, prints PASS or FAIL and calls get_tree().quit(code). From a terminal: check_integrator.gd extends SceneTree, run with godot --headless --script; on Windows use the _console.exe build, or read the exit code with 'echo $LASTEXITCODE' in PowerShell. A two-line terminal primer: cd into the project; run the command. Predict the result first; then break the accumulator on purpose and see the check fail.
workshops.check: Exit code 0 on the correct integrator.
workshops.contrast: Exit code 1 on the broken one (the negative test that proves the check bites).
workshops.basis: [M] every forces hall ships a headless probe (probe_field_receivers 39 checks, probe_gravity_relations 51; both UNTRACKED); test.checks is never taught. [M] commons/testing holds 931 scripts; no GUT or gdUnit is installed. [M] CLAUDE.md: the Desktop v4.6 exe is 'non-console'.

workshops.title: An imported body that moves
workshops.reason: The first hall whose primary is a skeleton. Critique #6 asks for import and animation before Soft Bodies for character-focused learners.
workshops.make: Import a rigged CC0 glTF character; play its clips in the AnimationPlayer; an AnimationTree blend (idle to walk) driven by the learner's player velocity; read a bone through a BoneAttachment3D.
workshops.contrast: get_bone_global_pose() ignores the IK modifier; the BoneAttachment3D reading does not.
workshops.basis: [M] VFM_09_Legs' primary is a Skeleton3D with FABRIK3D legs; AnimationTree appears in 6 files. [M memory] bone poses hide the modifier.

workshops.title: Release
workshops.reason: PostCrisis_Synthesis is kind assembly, whose make is 'A first independent work built from selected earlier capabilities'. The release completes that work; it adds no new capability, only returns. Distribution already appeared at W06 and CP3.
workshops.make: Desktop and (xr route) Quest builds with explicit include/exclude filters; the settings file becomes versioned and atomic (write settings.tmp, then rename; a version field; validation and a named fallback on load); credits with licences; a tagged release; instructions for a player outside the developer's machine.
workshops.check: A person who has never seen the project installs, plays, changes a setting and finds it kept. A settings file from the previous version loads or falls back by name.
workshops.contrast: A build missing a runtime data file because of a filter. A write killed half-way leaves the old settings intact.
workshops.basis: [M] the spine's last tutorial ends on a proposed experiment, not a release; the course project has no desktop preset. AssemblyPoseRecord.gd already writes through .tmp and rename.
